events.title: The Third Council of Constantinople condemns Pope Honorius I as a heretic
events.description: In its seventeenth session, the Third Council of Constantinople decreed that the late Pope Honorius I had spread the heresy of the one will, monothelitism. The council condemned monothelitism and defined Christ as having two wills.

events.title: Owain Glyndŵr is proclaimed Prince of Wales
events.description: Supporters at Glyndyfrdwy proclaimed Owain Glyndŵr Prince of Wales, launching a revolt against English rule. For several years he controlled much of Wales and summoned Welsh parliaments.

events.title: The infante Ferdinand takes Antequera from the Emirate of Granada
events.description: After a long siege, Antequera, a frontier stronghold of the Emirate of Granada, capitulated to a Castilian army led by the infante Ferdinand of Trastámara. He was known thereafter as Ferdinand of Antequera, and later became Ferdinand I of Aragon.

events.title: The Mayflower sails from Plymouth
events.description: The Mayflower left Plymouth with 102 passengers, Separatist 'Pilgrims' and others (6 September Old Style). After a gruelling crossing they founded Plymouth Colony in Massachusetts.

events.title: American troops defeat the British at the Battle of Harlem Heights
events.description: In the New York and New Jersey campaign, just under 1,800 American troops under General George Washington defeated just under 1,600 British troops under Brigadier-general Alexander Leslie on Harlem Heights, Manhattan.
events.html: In the New York and New Jersey campaign, just under 1,800 American troops under General George Washington defeated just under 1,600 British troops under Brigadier-general Alexander Leslie on Harlem Heights, Manhattan.

events.title: French and American forces begin the siege of Savannah
events.description: A joint Franco-American force set out to retake Savannah, Georgia, captured the year before by a British expeditionary corps under Lieutenant-Colonel Archibald Campbell. The siege, also called the second battle of Savannah, lasted until 18 October 1779.

events.title: Miguel Hidalgo's 'Grito de Dolores' launches Mexico's revolt
events.description: Priest Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell in Dolores and called his parishioners to rise against Spanish rule. Mexico celebrates the day as Independence Day, won in 1821.
events.html: Priest Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell in Dolores and called his parishioners to rise against Spanish rule. Mexico celebrates the day as Independence Day, won in 1821.

events.title: Robert College opens in Bebek with 31 students
events.description: Founded by the American philanthropist Christopher Robert and the missionary Cyrus Hamlin, Robert College opened with 31 students at Bebek Seminary School in Istanbul. It is the oldest continuously operating American school outside the United States.

events.title: William Durant incorporates General Motors
events.description: Buick head William Durant formed General Motors as a holding company, soon adding Oldsmobile, Cadillac and others. GM became for decades the world's largest car maker.

events.title: Phalangist militia begin the Sabra and Shatila massacre
events.description: Lebanese Christian militiamen entered Beirut's Sabra and Shatila refugee camps, in an area under Israeli control, and killed hundreds of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians over two days.
